key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the complainant's allegations that the respondent No. 2 had cheated him by demanding Rs. 2 Lakhs for the release of his buses and that the accused had committed offences under Sections 420, 406 and 161 IPC.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the complainant and two other witnesses as sufficient to support the summoning order for trial.

legal_representation.state: Anis Ahmed Khan, Shoaib Ahmad Khan, S.P. Singh, Chowdhari, Ramesh Kumar, Kamal Mohan Gupta

prosecution_argument: The complainant alleged that the respondent No. 2 cheated him, embezzled public money, and received illegal gratification by issuing directions to inspectors not to accept passengers tax, thereby committing offences under Sections 420, 406, and 161 of the Indian Penal Code.
defence_argument: The respondent No. 2 challenged the summoning order by filing a criminal revision, arguing that the sanction of the competent authority under Section 197 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was required for prosecuting a public servant for the alleged offences.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the offence of cheating under Section 420 IPC or related offences cannot be regarded as having been committed by a public servant while acting in discharge of official duty, thereby negating the requirement of sanction under Section 197 CrPC.
precedent_relied_upon: Rajendra Kumar Sitaram Pande and Others Vs. Uttam and Another 1999 (1) SCR 580; Prakash Singh Badal and Another Vs. State of Punjab and Others 2006 (10) Suppl. SCR 197
